clue.text: Angelic creature's unusual turn of phrase

indicators.note: an unusual turn gives the following word a strange new twist, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a heavenly being has an odd way of putting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' reads as one idiom, but it splits: 'unusual turn of' is the signal and 'phrase' is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels in Christian and Jewish tradition.

clue.text: Males dispersed in various directions as travellers?

indicators.note: things dispersed are scattered about, so all these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
south, east and north, three compass points

explanation.surface: Men scattering all over the place, going their separate ways like wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letters join the men in the mix; the question mark flags that travellers are of a particular commercial kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling salesmen are reps who journey from town to town selling goods, hence travellers, with a question mark for the narrowing.

clue.text: Deny admitting one learner put in new form

indicators.note: a word admitting others lets them inside it, so it wraps around what follows

blocks.note: to rebut a claim is to deny or refute it
Roman numeral one
L for learner, as on a UK learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Refusing to let in a novice, the whole thing is reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rebuilt has been constructed again, put back together in a new form.

clue.text: Craziness of incendiary extremes in party leading EU country

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, the first and the last

blocks.note: first and last letters of party
a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: Political madness: a firebrand party ahead of an election in a European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'leading' puts the party's ends on top of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is an obsessive compulsion to start fires, the mania of an arsonist or incendiary.

clue.text: Offer covering religious group, note, that's split down the middle

indicators.note: a word covering others lies over them on both sides, so it encloses them

blocks.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
a sect is a religious faction
a musical note

explanation.surface: An offer to a religious faction comes with a memo that divides opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal halves, exactly what splitting down the middle does.

clue.text: Daughter is framed by charge chosen at random

indicators.note: a picture framed by something sits inside its border, so the first words go within the later one

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
to incriminate is to charge someone with a crime

explanation.surface: A daughter is set up on a charge, picked out arbitrarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' tempts a criminal reading alongside 'charge', but here it just means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscriminate means done without careful selection, so made haphazardly or at random.

clue.text: Number wrongly repeated as three there

indicators.note: letters set out wrongly are in the wrong order and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
surface padding pointing out that the same letters recur
a second rearrangement of the same five letters, given as the repeat; the answer also runs across three there, a coincidence of that repetition

explanation.surface: Someone complains a figure has been mistakenly given twice as three in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure, but it is something that numbs. The same five letters can also be rearranged from 'there', which is the joke of 'repeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early general anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, so a number in the crossword sense.

clue.text: A live broadcast carried by television in Mediterranean city

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
a thing carried by something else is held within it

blocks.note: the usual short form of television
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A live programme is shown on TV from a city on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'television' sit together naturally, but only one of them supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is Israel's second-largest city, on its Mediterranean coastline.

clue.text: Far from vigilant as unknown weapon turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an algebraic unknown
a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A sentry is caught napping when a mystery weapon appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person is sleepy and inattentive, the opposite of being watchful and alert.

clue.text: Performance captured by artists even represented ability to draw

indicators.note: something represented is presented anew, so the letters are set out differently
a thing captured by another is held inside it

blocks.note: these eleven letters rearranged
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A display by artists shows even their talent for sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ability to draw' sounds like an artist's skill with a pencil, but it means pulling power or appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractiveness is the quality of drawing people in, the power to attract or pull others towards you.

clue.text: Criticise inside cover that's not bound by social conventions

indicators.note: inside places the first word within the one that follows

blocks.note: a lid covers a container
to berate is to criticise angrily

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a book jacket for being too free-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests a book's binding next to 'cover', but it means restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberated person is free of traditional constraints, emancipated from society's expectations.

clue.text: Male will ring and hear this?

definitions.text: Male will ring and hear this?

blocks.note: the male pronoun
the contraction of will, as in he'll
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man will make a phone call and expect a greeting at the other end.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the scene: when he rings, the first word he hears is the answer. HE'LL plus O spells it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard greeting when answering a telephone call.

clue.text: Person on diet near state of anger after gaining pound

indicators.note: gaining something means taking it in, so a letter is added inside

blocks.note: simmering is being close to boiling over with rage
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: A dieter gets close to fury after putting on a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's weight gain is ironic, since the answer is someone trying to lose it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimmer is someone trying to lose weight, typically by following a diet.

clue.text: Ringleader in English resort tries hard

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: the leader of ring is its first letter
St Ives is a seaside resort in Cornwall

explanation.surface: The head of a gang at a seaside town makes every effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' must be split into 'Ring' and 'leader'. St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, so strives means tries hard.

clue.text: Heard pronouncement of so-called college and scoffed

indicators.note: a pronouncement that is heard is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at a famous school's announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked, but it is the British slang for eating greedily. Eton is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to scoff food is to gobble it, so scoffed means eaten.

clue.text: Blood group, in short, I have that's aiding recovery

indicators.note: made short means trimmed, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the setter's intended word, cut short; the link from blood group is obscure
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A patient notes their blood type is a help in getting well.
explanation.walkthrough: The front of the answer is CURAT, a shortened CURATE, and I've completes it. How 'blood group' gives that word is unclear; it may be a slip for a clergy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curative has healing properties, so it helps a patient get better.

clue.text: Penetrating defensive position with soldier, perhaps

blocks.note: a trench is a dug-in defensive line
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: An infantryman breaches an entrenched line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier, perhaps' points to the insect, not a person: soldier ants are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comments are incisive and sharp, cutting deep, so penetrating.

clue.text: Part of team game in which a couple of universities combine

definitions.text: in which a couple of universities combine
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the blended name rather than a single noun

blocks.note: an ox is one animal in a team of draught oxen
the card game

explanation.surface: A section of a side plays a match where two universities join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' suggests sport, but here it is a yoked team of animals pulling a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge is the joint name blending Oxford and Cambridge, the two oldest English universities.

clue.text: Unorthodox belief in leaderless campaign's misplaced

indicators.note: without a leader the word loses its opening letter
misplaced letters are in the wrong places and must be rearranged

blocks.note: campaign's without its first letter, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A political campaign without a figurehead has put its faith in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism is a non-mainstream religion, a heterodox faith outside the established churches.

clue.text: A friend appearing on motorway radar, for example

blocks.note: taken as written
a crony is a close friend
M as in M1, the UK motorway prefix

explanation.surface: A mate shows up on a speed camera on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the friend above the motorway. Radar was coined from radio detection and ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is a word formed from initial letters, and radar is a famous example.

clue.text: Some business expenses for one of the county set

definitions.note: the county itself, not a member of its social set

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of them is taken, letters running across the gap

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a firm's outgoings goes on one of the landed gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'county set' is the British rural upper class; here it is read as the set of counties. Essex is a county north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the English counties, so one member of the set of counties.

clue.text: Travel over snow, with minimal temperature -– tricky stuff

blocks.note: to sleigh is to travel by sledge
the minimum of temperature: its first letter, or T as its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sledge ride in freezing weather can be treacherous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minimal temperature' suggests deep cold but just gives the symbol for temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is cunning dexterity, as in sleight of hand, the trickery of a conjuror.

clue.text: Became more moderate in a short time when retired?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the word at the end

blocks.note: having retired for the night, one is in bed
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone calmed down quickly after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests giving up work, but it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that abated lessened in intensity, as a storm dies down to something milder.

clue.text: Readable arrangement of lines, apart from chapter and verse

blocks.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
standard abbreviation for chapter
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A text whose lines can be read, except for its chapters and poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' and 'verse' suggest poetry, but the lines are printed stripes read by a scanner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar code is a pattern of parallel stripes that a machine scanner reads to identify a product.

clue.text: How marks may be given out a lot

blocks.clueFragment: How marks may be given out
blocks.note: test scores are given as a number out of a maximum; the words after out complete the phrase

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders about the way grades get handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks are given as a score out of ten; the clue's 'out' is completed by the two missing words, which run together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, many times, so a lot in the adverbial sense.

clue.text: Kind of family having eccentric uncle and aunt ridiculed, initially

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters go astray
initially means at the start, so only first letters are taken

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
first letters of aunt and ridiculed

explanation.surface: A household with an odd uncle and a mocked aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene of relatives hides that only the uncle is rearranged; the aunt and her ridicule give just initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear family is parents and children only, the household type without extended relatives.

clue.text: Conviction when Ecstasy's found in part of camp

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: tents make up a campsite
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone is convicted after drugs turn up at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' reads as a court verdict, but it means a firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle firmly held, a belief someone is convinced of.

clue.text: Cut off from West, rang editor

indicators.note: taking letters from a word means only part of it is used

blocks.note: the tail of this word
taken as written
standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone isolated from the West telephones a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' also hints at dropping the first letter of the next word, which is how EST comes from West.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged people are alienated from each other, having been cut off from a relationship.

clue.text: Portray as evil happening, surrounded by death

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed on all sides

blocks.note: demise is a formal word for death
what is on is taking place

explanation.surface: Depicting something wicked going on amid fatalities.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonise is to represent someone as a devil, wicked or threatening.

clue.text: Work of art, say, placed outside university

indicators.note: a thing placed outside another goes around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: to state is to say
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A sculpture, for instance, is installed outside a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb that gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a classic example of a work of art.
